The position provides responsive and professional technical support for computers, mobile devices, software, peripherals, network connectivity, accounts, and related technology services. Responsibilities include evaluating and addressing user needs; diagnosing and resolving hardware and software issues; installing, configuring, maintaining, and upgrading technology; coordinating equipment and software acquisitions; and providing individual and group training. Required Qualifications Bachelor's Degree required in a related area and / or equivalent experience / training. 1+ years supporting software installation and troubleshooting 3+ years experience communicating technical and non-technical information in a clear and concise manner to users at various levels with a wide range of experience. 1+ years Supporting higher education A/V technologies Evidence of a strong customer service focus. Proven track record of problem solving. Preferred Qualifications Self-motivated with a history of working effectively as an individual and as part of a team. Working knowledge of modern software technologies. Broad knowledge of IT-related products and services. Special Conditions Of Employment Occasional evening, weekend, and holiday work. Serves as a primary point of contact for technical assistance, promptly responding to service requests; diagnosing and resolving issues involving hardware, software, network connectivity, printing, file access, and other technology services; and keeping users informed throughout the resolution process. Installs, configures, deploys, maintains, and upgrades computers, operating systems, applications, and peripheral equipment in accordance with university security requirements and technology standards. Coordinates warranty repairs, vendor services, and other external maintenance as needed. Documents incidents, resolutions, configurations, and support procedures in the service management system and maintains accurate records of departmental equipment, software, licenses, warranties, and technology assets in accordance with university inventory and audit requirements. Assists with annual equipment inventories and coordinates the secure retirement and disposal of obsolete equipment. Researches and coordinates technology purchases, renewals, and vendor services; monitors equipment and software lifecycles; and advises appropriate staff of upcoming replacement, licensing, maintenance, and upgrade needs. Identifies opportunities to improve service delivery, system reliability, security, and cost-effectiveness. Also provides technical support for departmental meetings, presentations, audiovisual systems, shared office technologies, and other equipment and services supported by AAIT. Applications Support (30%): Serves as a primary technical contact for users of campus-wide web applications supported by AAIT. Receives, documents, prioritizes, and resolves service requests; provides guidance on application functionality, procedures, and appropriate system use; and keeps users informed throughout the resolution process. Collaborates with campus departments, functional owners, developers, and other technical staff to address application, workflow, and policy-related questions. Investigates and documents system issues, communicates problems and requested enhancements to development staff, and coordinates follow-up through resolution. Participates in the testing and implementation of new applications, system enhancements, upgrades, and process changes. Reviews system submissions, reports, and other outputs to verify that they function as intended and meet established campus requirements. Website Maintenance (15%): Assists with the maintenance and continuous improvement of departmental websites and web applications serving campus-wide audiences. Creates, updates, and publishes accessible digital content using content management systems. Recommends improvements to site organization, visual design, navigation, usability, and the overall user experience; monitors and responds to website inquiries; and collaborates with system administrators and application developers to address configuration, functionality, performance, and security concerns. Uses web analytics and other available data to evaluate site activity, identify trends, and recommend content or service improvements. Works with campus accessibility professionals and content owners to identify and remediate barriers and support compliance with applicable digital accessibility standards. Documents testing results, communicates issues to technical and functional stakeholders, verifies corrective changes, and recommends improvements to the accessibility, security, reliability, and usability of AAIT-supported digital services. Training and Documentation (15%): Develops and delivers training for AAIT-supported applications, technologies, systems, and services used by faculty and staff. Advises users on operating systems, productivity and collaboration tools, data and spreadsheet applications, web browsers, digital media and content-publishing tools, Adobe applications, and other supported technologies. Creates and maintains clear, accessible user guides, instructional materials, procedures, and internal operational documentation, updating these resources as systems and practices evolve. Supports departmental purchasing activities through Gateway and serves as a FlexCard cardholder in accordance with university policies and procedures. Maintains current knowledge of relevant technologies, security practices, accessibility requirements, and industry standards through research, training, and professional development. Responsibilities Job Duty 1 - Provide advanced technical support for complex hardware and software issues, diagnosing problems and implementing effective solutions. Job Duty 2 - Document technical processes, configurations, and solutions to create a knowledge base that supports continuous improvement in support services. Job Duty 3 - Assist in the development and implementation of Information Technology policies, procedures, and standards to ensure consistent and effective support operations. Job Duty 4 - Conduct training sessions for other Information Technology staff and end-users on technical topics, promoting knowledge sharing and skill development within the team. Job Duty 5 - Monitor and analyze system performance, identifying trends and potential issues to proactively address them before they impact users. Job Duty 6 - Stay informed about emerging technologies and industry trends, evaluating their potential impact on the institution and recommending adoption as appropriate. Job Duty 7 - Participate in project teams to implement new technology solutions, providing technical expertise and support throughout the project lifecycle. Job Duty 8 - Prepare and present reports on support activities, metrics, and system performance to management, highlighting successes and areas for improvement. Job Duty 9 - Collaborate with Information Technology teams to troubleshoot and resolve incidents that require specialized knowledge and expertise in technology systems. Job Duty 10 - Perform other job-related duties as assigned. Experience installing, calibrating, or troubleshooting industrial cameras, depth sensors, motion-capture systems, or other machine-vision equipment. Familiarity with ROS/ROS 2, Docker, NVIDIA Jetson or similar edge-computing platforms, and deployment of computer-vision or AI applications. Familiarity with XR/VR/AR/MR systems, spatial-computing devices, tracking systems, haptic devices, 3D scanners, or related research instrumentation; familiarity with Unity, Unreal Engine, OpenXR, or vendor XR development tools. Strong organizational and documentation skills, with attention to configuration management, maintenance records, and operational readiness.
